name: Tesora
tagline: MySQL-protocol sharding layer (ex-ParElastic) and OpenStack Trove DBaaS vendor; bought by Stratoscale in 2017.
description: Tesora started in 2010 as ParElastic, whose Database Virtualization Engine (DVE) sat between applications and a pool of MySQL or MariaDB servers, exposing one virtual MySQL-protocol database while transparently sharding data across storage nodes with ACID transactions across them. Renamed Tesora, the company open-sourced DVE under the AGPL in 2014 and shifted to an enterprise distribution of OpenStack Trove, the OpenStack database-as-a-service, becoming its leading contributor. Stratoscale acquired Tesora in February 2017 to build AWS-style database services, and both DVE and the Tesora DBaaS platform stopped as standalone products. For transparent MySQL sharding today, look at Vitess or a distributed SQL database.
statusNote: Acquired by Stratoscale in February 2017; the DVE repo has been idle since 2015 and Tesora products are no longer offered. Use Vitess, TiDB or PlanetScale.

pricing.notes: DVE community source remains on GitHub; commercial editions and the DBaaS platform ended after the acquisition.

scale.notes: Scale-out by adding MySQL storage nodes behind the virtualization engine.

strengths: Applications saw one MySQL database while data was sharded underneath
Cross-shard ACID transactions without application changes
Ran on standard MySQL or MariaDB servers
weaknesses: Discontinued after the 2017 acquisition; code idle since 2015
Extra proxy hop and query-routing overhead
AGPL community edition with a tiny user base
useCases: Historical reference for MySQL sharding middleware
